questions: Is the patient a child (under 18)?
Has there been any recent infection (e.g., viral illness) in the weeks before the eye movements started?
Is there any associated jerking or trembling of the arms, legs, or body (myoclonus)?
Is there unsteadiness of gait or clumsiness (ataxia)?
Are the abnormal eye movements continuous and chaotic in all directions (opsoclonus)?
Is the patient currently taking any medications (e.g., anticonvulsants, alcohol)?
Is there a history of seizures?
Is the eye movement a to-and-fro oscillation (pendular nystagmus) that worsens on side gaze?
Is the patient dizzy or experiencing vertigo?
Is there associated hearing loss, tinnitus, or ear fullness?
Does the nystagmus beat in a specific direction (e.g., horizontal, unidirectional) and is suppressed by visual fixation?
Does the nystagmus change direction when the gaze is shifted (gaze-evoked nystagmus)?
Is there weakness in the arms or legs?
Is the nystagmus predominantly vertical (upbeat or downbeat)?
Is there any facial droop, double vision, or ptosis?
Is there decreased sensation in the hands or feet?
Was the onset of symptoms (vertigo, ataxia) sudden/acute (over hours to days)?
Is there any slurring of speech (dysarthria) or difficulty swallowing?
Does the patient consume alcohol heavily or have a history of alcohol abuse?
Has there been any associated headache or vomiting?
